name: al-Harith ibn Hillizah
bio: Al-Harith ibn Hillizah, of Yashkur, a branch of Bakr ibn Wa'il, was a contemporary of King 'Amr ibn Hind of al-Hirah (A.D. 554-69). His Mu'allaqa is held in the Mu'allaqat collection on this site and is not repeated here.
Two other pieces by him are in the Mufaddaliyat, Odes XXV and LXII, which are given here in Lyall's translation.

poems.title: Ode XXV: Whose were the dwellings, all but
poems.author: al-Harith ibn Hillizah
poems.note: Lyall's heading: al-Harith son of Hillizah, of Yashkur.
poems.text:
Whose were the dwellings, all but faded out, at al-Hubs, the traces of which are like the written sheets of the Persians ?

Nought is to be seen there save the herds of wild kine, black-cheeked, [their white backs] shining in the sun,

Or the foot-prints of the noble steeds in the sides of the higher ground, and the marks of their trampling there.

I stayed my comrades there, as I revolved all my memories of things past — and I was ever a man to dream !

Until, when the gazelles wrapped themselves in the skirts of the shade, and sought the noon-tide shelters they had made [by the roots of trees] ,

And I lost all hope of that which I had longed for with pain from her — and nothing brings trouble of mind to an end like hopelessness—

I betook myself to a she-camel, lean and muscular, as strong as a male, who shatters the stones with the blows of her short rounded feet,

With the leather shoon cut through by long wear — the rags of them fly about like morsels of fur in the rugged level plains.

Wilt thou not then direct her course to a King of good judgement in the shepherding of his people, glorious of soul —

To the Son of Mariyah, the generous — nay, is there any peer to the Father of Hassan among mankind ?

He bestows on thee ample coats of mail, swelling out over the girdles that hold them in at the waist, and black horses [tall] as palm-trees,

And ingots of yellow gold which he gives by twos, and slave-girls, some white, others with a violet tinge in the inner lip.

He gives no thought to his wealth as he deals it around : to him a lucky star and an unlucky are all one ;

And for him goes up the prayer there, never against him, what time the noses of men are abased as they stumble in the dust.

poems.title: Ode LXII: Darkling the wraith came flitting by
poems.author: al-Harith ibn Hillizah
poems.note: Lyall's heading: The same. Lyall: a short piece consisting of three fragments. Al-Harith's Mu'allaqa is held in the Mu'allaqat collection.
poems.text:
Darkling the wraith came flitting by — what a wonder-night! and it glided on to where lay our saddles, but would not stay.

How didst thou find to our camp the path? never strong afoot wast thou, and we through Sagsag's ridges had pushed our way,

And our train was slow at the journey's end, and their beasts were spent, save one swift-foot for the women's litter was set apart.

Full many cups have I quaffed of wine when the feast was spread : full many deer have I frighted, riding a long-backed steed:

White they as pearls in the valley-bend, and my horse a hawk driving before him a pack of doves to the box-thorn bush —

As a hawk that hunts with his talons, deft on the wing to strike : when he clutches once in his swoop a dove, she moves no more !

Yea and if thou ask they will tell thee how when the host falls back, and the coward bears in his face the sign of his shrinking heart,

Our swords rain down on their heads a torrent of shattering blows, as the hail-storm batters the leather tent stretched taut with ropes.

And when afternoon brings home the camels in winter days, tripping short steps as they hurry in to the wattled booth,

Thou shalt find our cheer for the guest the best that the tribes can show : if milk there be not, we sit down straight to the arrow-game.
